newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW workers urge increased job creation.
newsitem.headline: VW workers urge increased job creation.

text.p: Works council leaders at Volkswagen AG, Europe's largest car-maker, on Thursday called on management to take on more staff to deal with what they called the "outstanding demand" for its cars.

"Even if only through temporary positions, we want to use the outstanding position of VW in all its markets both to secure existing employment and make a contribution towards the current mass jobless levels," VW works council chief Klaus Volkert said in a statement.
He said that demand was currently being satisfied "to an overwhelming extent" by overtime and weekend work among the 90,000 employees at VW's six plants.
Unemployment in parts of the region around its main Wolfsburg facility in the state of Lower Saxony meanwhile stood at around 18 percent, Volkert said.
VW said at the Geneva motor show earlier this month that group sales rose 13 percent to about 660,000 vehicles in February and that sales so far for the year were doing well.
Incoming orders in Germany for the first two months of 1997 were up 30 percent and above expectations, the group said.
Volkert said the works council was now holding negotiations on staff increases with the management.
Separately, wage negotiators at VW said on Wendesday that the latest round in pay talks had ended without an agreement.
Under discussion is a plan designed to allow early retirement by staff while maintaining employee and company contributions towards pensions up until the standard 65-year-old retirement age.
